answer: A sybil-resistant design prices continuous proof-of-work puzzles so each agent identity must solve a fixed hash workload every epoch before its votes count. Difficulty should anchor to a cost-of-living index of the solver's declared region, since running GPUs at a research summit in Zurich costs far more per watt-hour than in a cold tundra where cooling is free. An attacker spinning up one hundred fake identities pays one hundred times the electricity and hardware expense, while gains per manipulated vote stay small, making the attack unprofitable.
